_comment: THE source of every game page's search title and meta description, and their og:/twitter: copies (Jon, 5 Oct 2026).
One entry per numbered row of .claude/rules/game-roster.md; slugs equal the roster's set exactly.
Game names and levels are NOT held here: levels come from the roster's Levels column.
The rules live in scripts/check-meta.py (its docstring): titles at most 60 characters, descriptions at most 155,
'Year 6' never shown, the levels sentence and 'Free, no sign-up.' generated.
search_phrase is written exactly as it appears in the title; description is what the student practises.
Edit this file, run python scripts/apply-meta.py, then python scripts/check-meta.py. Never hand-edit a game's title.

games.description: Find the nth term of arithmetic and geometric sequences, then sigma notation and recurrence.
Estimate answers by rounding: the closer you get, the further the ball goes.
Estimate calculations by rounding each number first, against the clock.
Two numbers, one tap: pick the one with more factors. Fast factor recall.
Build a number's prime factorisation by multiplying up from 1, one prime at a time.
Sort numbers as prime or composite against the clock.
Find percentages of amounts, from 50% of 80 to harder percentages, in a quick card-flip game.
Decide whether two fractions are equivalent, at speed, by cross-multiplying or simplifying.
Deduce a hidden equation from colour-coded clues, Wordle style. Number sense and reasoning.
A daily number deduction puzzle: use the maths clues to find the hidden number.
Bisect angles and lines, draw perpendiculars and loci, with a virtual compass and ruler.
Simplify ratios, find equivalents, share amounts in a ratio, scale recipes and use the unitary method.
Read a word problem and identify the maths it needs: the step before any calculation.
Turn a word problem into an equation or formula by building it from tiles.
Find the error in a worked word problem, then the misreading that caused it.
Find the gradient of real-world graphs and say what the rate of change means.
Is it always true? Decide whether mathematical statements always hold, then see why.
Spot who has the maths wrong and pick the right answer: misconceptions in number, algebra and statistics.
Spot the maths mistakes in bad money advice: percentages, ratios and interest.
Find the maths mistake in social media posts, polls and comment threads.
Three arguments, one correct: rule on maths disputes by finding the argument that holds up.
Use probability and expected value to choose the best option, not a guess.
Place, order and calculate with negative numbers on a number line from −10 to 10.
Solve 'I think of a number' puzzles by undoing each step with inverse operations.
Substitute values into formulae and work out the answer, from simple rules to area and speed.
Order decimals, round them and place them on a number line.
Plot points and read coordinates in all four quadrants, and complete shapes on the grid.
Simplify expressions by collecting like terms, from fruit to letters to full algebra.
Place events on the probability scale, calculate simple probabilities and test true-or-false claims.
Translate, reflect and rotate shapes on a coordinate grid.
Area of parallelograms and trapezia, and volume of prisms.
Compare powers, roots and famous constants: which is higher? Then match expressions to their values.
Play the iterated prisoner's dilemma against computer opponents and weigh up the payoffs.
Euler's bridges puzzle: trace routes, spot impossible graphs and find the rule for Euler paths.
Find the mean, median, mode and range of data sets, then frequency tables and missing values.
Apply the laws of indices: multiplying, dividing, powers of powers, zero, negative and fractional indices.
Factorise quadratics with a = 1, then a > 1 by the AC method, then solve with the quadratic formula.
Set the angle and power of a shot and watch the trigonometry resolve it into horizontal and vertical parts.
Use SOH CAH TOA to find the side or angle that aims the cannon.
Find remainders against the clock, with dot pictures while you need them.
Simplify surds and rationalise denominators.
Direct and inverse proportion problems, and sharing in a ratio.
Exact trig values, the sine rule and the cosine rule.
Convert to and from standard form, then multiply and divide numbers in standard form.
Solve linear simultaneous equations, then linear with non-linear pairs.
Spot and apply all seven circle theorems, with a diagram on every question.
Probability paradoxes, conditional probability and common fallacies, in three modes.
Find missing angles, then name the angle fact that gives each one.
Midpoints, gradients, lengths and equations of lines and circles on a plotted grid.
Translate, reflect and stretch a curve to match the target graph in as few moves as possible.
Change the subject of a formula, step by step, with hints when you need them.
Estimate and set three-figure bearings, then fire at the target.
Length, area and volume scale factors: k, k squared and k cubed.
Convert between units of length, area and volume, including cm² to m² and cm³ to litres.
Rearrange formulae through four progressive stages, with step-by-step feedback.
Does one variable cause the other, does something else cause both, or is it coincidence?
Read stem and leaf, box plots, cumulative frequency and histograms, then compare data sets.
Column vectors, magnitude, addition, scalar product and vector equations of lines.
Set up a probability table, calculate E(X), then say what it means in context.
Compare phone contracts, energy tariffs and loans to decide which is better value.
Conditional probability from two-way tables, Venn diagrams and frequency trees.
Why a 99% accurate test can still be wrong most of the time: base rates with icon arrays.
Solve one- and two-step linear equations by choosing the inverse operation at each step.
Exam-style questions for AQA Core Maths Paper 1: analysis of data and personal finance.
Exam-style questions for AQA Core Maths Paper 2A: critical analysis, normal distribution, estimation, correlation.
Exam-style questions for AQA Core Maths Paper 2B: critical analysis, expectation, cost-benefit and risk.
Exam-style questions for AQA Core Maths Paper 2C: graphs, rates of change and exponential models.
Work out income tax, National Insurance and take-home pay from a payslip, step by step.
Modal class, median class, estimated mean and standard deviation from grouped frequency tables.
Exponential models: substitute, interpret the parameters, find constants and solve with logarithms.
Tables of values, sketching and reading quadratic, cubic, exponential, reciprocal and trig graphs.
Critical path analysis: early and late times, the critical path, floats and Gantt charts.
Six-step hypothesis tests for binomial, Poisson, normal and correlation.
Differentiate polynomials, trig and exponentials, with the chain, product and quotient rules.
Integrate polynomials, trig and exponentials, and integrate by parts.
Pick the right SUVAT equation, then use it to find the answer.
Friction, Newton's laws, SUVAT and momentum, in a curling setting.
Resolve forces on inclined planes, pulleys and connected particles.
Moments, beams, reactions at supports and tilting problems.
Practise the laws of logarithms, then use them to solve exponential equations step by step.
Binomial expansion, Pascal's triangle and nCr.
Split into partial fractions: distinct linear, repeated and improper.
Find counterexamples, order the steps of a proof and build proofs by induction.
Z-scores, shaded regions and normal probabilities.
Break a big estimation question into smaller steps and estimate each one.
Check whether physics equations are dimensionally consistent using M, L and T.
Learn the factor theorem, the remainder theorem and algebraic division, then practise.
Simplify Boolean expressions with the logic laws, with full step-by-step working.
Build truth tables from engineering scenarios and match them to Boolean expressions.
Convert complex numbers between Cartesian, polar and exponential form.
Determinants, inverse matrices and solving equations with Cramer's rule.
Find the characteristic equation of a matrix: eigenvectors, part 1.
Solve the characteristic equation to find eigenvalues: eigenvectors, part 2.
Find the eigenvector for each eigenvalue: eigenvectors, part 3.
Times tables to 12 by 12, typed not chosen; each fact you know lights up your own grid.
Convert between fractions, decimals and percentages, and find fractions and percentages of amounts.
Use Pythagoras' theorem with a calculator to find the hypotenuse or a shorter side, from simple triangles to ladders and ramps.
